A1.justification: Both PDFs, including their appendices, are readable and describe the same research work. SliceLens becomes GH-ESD and FeSD becomes GESD; matching the methods, datasets and detailed result tables supports reliable comparison despite extensive reorganization.

before.justification: V1 reports original slice-discovery evaluations, component ablations, and classification and detection model-repair experiments in Section 5 and Appendix B.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and reports additional HiBug2 comparisons, verification examples and dataset analyses in Section 5 and Appendices B–C.

M1.justification: The core hypothesis generation, grounded VLM matching and maximum-local-slope verification pipeline remains. Small procedural refinements include explicitly requesting object interactions and changing the attribute-inference prompt from at least four refinement turns to three (v1 Figure 10; v2 Figure 9). V2 also introduces Spearman correlation as an alternative verification statistic without replacing the default slope procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same COCO, KITTI and face-detection sources, 21 detection and 21 segmentation slices, Waterbirds, CelebA, NICO++, and COCO bicycle repair data. GESD renames FeSD. The added examples and distribution analyses concern existing coverage.

E2.justification: V2 Table 1 adds HiBug2 to the principal detection comparison, alongside retained FACTS* and HiBug*. This materially strengthens the comparison: HiBug2 scores 0.63 versus the previous strongest baseline's 0.31. The semantic hypothesis-versus-tags ablation also replaces HiBug* with HiBug2. Classification and repair comparator sets remain unchanged.

E3.justification: FACTS preprocessing is described differently: v1 Section 5.2 aggregates instance errors into an image-level error rate, whereas v2 Section 5 labels an entire image erroneous whenever any bounding box has an error. This constitutes a reported protocol revision, without establishing that experiments were rerun. The main evaluation metrics, training settings and repair budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: V2 adds accepted, rejected and inconclusive hypothesis case studies, dataset error-count and conditional-error-rate analyses (Appendix B, Figures 15–16), and a qualitative Spearman verification check. The tag ablation is revised around HiBug2. Existing grounding, threshold-sensitivity and model-choice analyses are largely retained; the Spearman addition lacks numerical results.

E5.justification: Both versions report ten independent classification-repair runs and three detection-repair repetitions, retain the same uncertainty values, and describe seed randomization for standard deviations. No new confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-reporting practice appears. The alternative verification statistic concerns the discovery method rather than experimental uncertainty.

E6.justification: The new HiBug2 result of 0.63 materially changes the principal comparison against the retained 0.73. The semantic ablation replaces HiBug* precision/recall of 0.54/0.57 with HiBug2's 0.36/0.71, representing different comparators. Category summaries also change: the proposed method's contextual-interference and intrinsic-difficulty scores move from 0.70/0.76 to 0.75/0.73 (v1 Figure 4; v2 Figure 3), without explanation. Detailed Tables 7–8, classification scores and repair results remain numerically unchanged.

T1.justification: V2 Section 3.1 adds a formal evaluation-unit domain encompassing correct instances, false positives, false negatives, discrepancy regions and whole images, together with an explicit expected-loss formulation of subgroup selection. This is a limited formal addition. The VLM normalization, underlying slope criterion and GroupDRO equations are retained; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The framework, grounded benchmark and actionable model-repair contributions remain. The abstract and introduction revise the headline detection advantage from 0.42 over HiBug* to 0.10 over HiBug2 and explicitly distinguish detection results from supporting segmentation evidence. The benchmark-first claim is now qualified by 'to our knowledge.'

C2.justification: V2 explicitly acknowledges that overwriting non-slice predictions creates synthetic perfect annotations and limits evaluation to predefined failures. It adds limitations from dataset bias and underrepresented failure modes, plus explanations concerning hallucinated matches and relational tag limitations. The earlier concern about incomplete hypothesis coverage remains, with expanded discussion of human involvement.

D1.justification: V2 newly specifies verification defaults of gamma = 0.5 and trend threshold = 0.2, gives a five-unit minimum-window example, and documents three experienced researchers defining slices. It clarifies fixed models in the grounding ablation and promises dataset release upon acceptance. These disclosures do not establish changed settings or current public availability; most implementation and repair details are retained.

R1.justification: Related work retains the principal competing methods but more explicitly contrasts their image-level error evaluation and atomic tags with grounded relational hypotheses. Eight peripheral references are removed, including MedSegBench, Hidden Stratification and Just Train Twice, alongside shortened medical and fairness discussion. No new cited research is introduced.

P1.justification: The main paper is extensively rewritten, with new terminology, a separate problem formulation, reorganized method subsections and stronger emphasis on instance-level evaluation. Detection experiments now precede classification experiments, repair sections are reordered, and the appendices gain a dedicated dataset-details section. These changes substantially alter the narrative beyond renaming.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column presentation, with substantially redrawn introductory and pipeline diagrams. V2 expands the category chart, revises the tag illustration, adds verification examples and two dataset-statistics figures, and removes the earlier benchmark-comparison and face-grounding illustrations. Prompt displays and tables are redistributed. Repeated 'Title Suppressed Due to Excessive Length' running headers introduce a formatting defect.

improvement.justification: The HiBug2 comparison provides a stronger test of the central claim and appropriately reduces the headline advantage from 0.42 to 0.10. Newly disclosed verification settings and clearer benchmark limitations improve reproducibility and interpretation. These benefits outweigh limited reporting weaknesses, including unexplained category-score revisions and an unquantified Spearman check. Most underlying experiments and results remain unchanged, so the overall gain is limited.
